evidence: The revert claim was wrong: the agent showed install.sh's cmp branch reporting the workflow 'is up to date', so the template had already been updated outside the repo. The kernel was real, though. The old header named 'agent-code-review-setup/install.sh' without saying where it lives, so the agent answered already-fixed on the revert and fixed the header pointer.
guidance_note: When a generated file's template lives outside the repo, the original header should give a location any reader can resolve, such as a public repo URL, not a bare tool name.

evidence: Fix commit 1f82219 replaced the vague pointer with '~/.claude/skills/agent-code-review-setup/install.sh', which resolves on only one machine. It also added the sentence 'this says where it is, so it can actually be reached', so the F1 fix repeated the defect it set out to fix. The agent switched to the public dotfiles URL in db8d291.
guidance_note: When fixing an unfindable pointer in a public repo, point at a location every reader can resolve (a URL) and do not add sentences asserting that the pointer works.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. db8d291 only touched the header, while the 'version lives on the uses: line and nowhere else' comment was already in the original round-0 hunk. The sibling comment 'Pinned to the moving `v1` tag' did contradict that principle, and the agent stripped the literal and checked with grep.
guidance_note: Before writing a comment that states a file-wide rule, grep the file for existing violations of that rule and fix them in the same commit.

evidence: db8d291, the F2 fix, added the parenthetical 'that copy is a symlink into the repo above, not a separate source'. That claim is about one machine's filesystem and no reader of this repo can check it, which is the same unverifiable-assertion pattern F2 removed. The agent deleted it instead of hedging it.
guidance_note: When a fix removes an unverifiable claim, do not add another; a pointer comment should hold only the pointer.

narrative: The reviewer's first premise, that the generated file was hand-edited and would be reverted, was wrong; the installer reported it up to date. The agent turned the kernel (the header never said where the template lives) into a header fix. That fix used a machine-local path plus a reachability claim, and the next fix added an unverifiable symlink claim, so each fix spawned the next finding. F3 was a pre-existing inconsistency the reviewer only noticed in round 2.
guidance_observations: Each header fix added sentences to defend the previous sentence; writing the minimal pointer (a URL only) on the first fix would have closed the thread in one round.
The agent verified the URL with curl before committing the second fix, which is the check the first fix lacked.

evidence: `_flag_difference` returned `" ".join(sorted(left - right))`, which is empty when the declared side has nothing unique, and `_reject_restatement` renders an empty declared side as '(unset)'. That reads as 'no flags set' for a profile that has `--a=1`. The fix in 9507637 renders full effective values, the reviewer's own suggestion, and drops the launch-policy layer from this comparison.
guidance_note: Before returning a new value shape into a shared message template, read how the template renders each empty or None side.

evidence: In the diff, `parsed = flags.layer(raw, ...)` runs before the RESERVED_SWITCHES loop. A duplicated `--user-data-dir` would therefore get the comma-join remedy, which fails again on reload. 9507637 moved the reserved scan back in front and added a test.
guidance_note: When inserting a new check ahead of an existing one, list the inputs both checks reject and confirm the first message's remedy still works for each.

evidence: This duplicates F2: same ordering, same misleading remedy `--user-data-dir=/a,/b`. Both were fixed in 9507637, which scans `Flag.parse` for reserved switches before `flags.layer`.
guidance_note: When inserting a new check ahead of an existing one, list the inputs both checks reject and confirm the first message's remedy still works for each.

evidence: This duplicates F1, with a cleaner repro: declared `--a=1`, asked `--a=1 --b=2`, so `left-right` is empty and the message reads 'declared (unset)'. The full-value rendering fix in 9507637 removes the empty side.
guidance_note: Before returning a new value shape into a shared message template, read how the template renders each empty or None side.

evidence: For `--foo --foo=bar`, `_joined` keeps only the non-None values and suggests `--foo=bar` as the 'comma-joined' fix, which silently discards the bare form. The agent replaced it with `_remedy` keyed on value count. That rewrite still left the F11 phrasing defect and the F15 identical-duplicate case.
guidance_note: Before writing a message that suggests a fix computed from inputs, write out every input-shape pair (identical, both valued, mixed, both bare) and check the suggestion for each.

evidence: `" ".join(sorted(right - left)) if asked else None` yields "" when the request only drops a declared flag. The template has no fallback for the asked side, so the message trails off at 'you asked for '. Full-value rendering in 9507637 fixed it.
guidance_note: Before returning a new value shape into a shared message template, read how the template renders each empty or None side.

evidence: This duplicates F6: declared `--a=1 --b=1`, asked `--a=1` gives a blank asked side. The same fix covers it, pinned by test_dropping_a_declared_flag_is_refused_without_trailing_off.
guidance_note: Before returning a new value shape into a shared message template, read how the template renders each empty or None side.

evidence: 9507637, the F1 fix, removed the only `LAUNCH_POLICY_FLAGS` use in cli.py (the `_flag_difference` compose call) but left the import. The agent's grep confirmed it was dead. The agent also noted its ruff run used `--select` and so excluded F401.
guidance_note: When a fix deletes the last use of a name, run the linter unfiltered (F401 included) on the changed files before pushing.

evidence: This duplicates F8 on the same line: the dead `LAUNCH_POLICY_FLAGS` import left behind when 9507637 dropped the policy layer from `_effective_flags`. It was removed in 90223e2.
guidance_note: When a fix deletes the last use of a name, run the linter unfiltered (F401 included) on the changed files before pushing.

evidence: This duplicates F8: the dead import after 9507637. It is removed in 90223e2.
guidance_note: When a fix deletes the last use of a name, run the linter unfiltered (F401 included) on the changed files before pushing.

evidence: 9507637's `_remedy` branch for `len(values) == 1` says 'or comma-join the values if you meant both', but that branch has only one value. So the F5 fix still misled on the mixed case it was written for. 90223e2 dropped the clause and re-keyed the branches on shape.
guidance_note: Before writing a message that suggests a fix computed from inputs, write out every input-shape pair (identical, both valued, mixed, both bare) and check the suggestion for each.

evidence: This is the fourth report of the same dead `LAUNCH_POLICY_FLAGS` import, orphaned by the F1 fix in 9507637. It is removed in 90223e2.
guidance_note: When a fix deletes the last use of a name, run the linter unfiltered (F401 included) on the changed files before pushing.

evidence: The resolve.py comment says the compose call is 'the same call `crom add` compares against'. After 9507637 made `_effective_flags` compose only `(scope.default_flags, stanza)`, resolve_spec still composes three layers, so the comment became false. The agent rewrote it to name the different layer sets.
guidance_note: When a fix changes what a function composes, grep for comments elsewhere that claim parity with it and update them in the same commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. 9507637 does not touch resolve.py, and the 'every layer's text is checked' comment is in the original diff. The documented behavior (a `${TYPO}` in an overridden defaults flag still raises) had no test. The agent added test_an_unknown_variable_is_caught_even_in_a_flag_that_gets_overridden, even though the reply-hint says pushback.
guidance_note: When a comment declares a non-obvious behavior intentional, add the test that pins it in the same commit.

evidence: `flags = ["--foo=bar", "--foo=bar"]` yields `--foo=bar,bar` in both the original `_joined` (it joined all non-None values) and 9507637's `_remedy`. The defect predates the fix rather than being caused by it, though the F5 fix's claimed enumeration of shapes missed it. 90223e2 added a `first == second` arm.
guidance_note: Before writing a message that suggests a fix computed from inputs, write out every input-shape pair (identical, both valued, mixed, both bare) and check the suggestion for each.

narrative: Round 0 found real defects: the diff-shaped flags rendering produced '(unset)' and a blank asked side, the reserved-check ordering regressed, and the duplicate remedy text was wrong. The fix for the rendering dropped the launch-policy layer but left a dead import (reported four times) and a stale parity comment in resolve.py. The remedy rewrite kept a misleading clause, and the identical-duplicate case it missed predated it. Round 1 also carried the independent F14, so a second fix round was needed regardless.
guidance_observations: A filtered ruff invocation (`--select RUF010,I001,E501`) hid an F401 the fix created; the agent should lint changed files unfiltered after every fix.
Changing a comparison's layer set should trigger a grep for comments elsewhere that assert parity with it.
The reviewer posted the same finding up to four times per line, which inflates finding counts without adding rounds.

evidence: The PR adds `--disable-features`/`--enable-features` to RESERVED_SWITCHES, so a `flags` list can no longer name them. The model.py comment using `--disable-features` as the compose example therefore describes an input the parser rejects. The agent fixed all three sites (cli.py, model.py, resolve.py) in 73f9e64.
guidance_note: When reserving a switch, grep comments and docstrings for that switch used as an example and update them in the same commit.

evidence: This duplicates F1 on the same line, and it additionally names the resolve.py:265 comment. Fixed in the same three-site pass.
guidance_note: When reserving a switch, grep comments and docstrings for that switch used as an example and update them in the same commit.

evidence: The check `if not name.strip() or "," in name` does pass `" Foo"` verbatim into the comma-joined switch. Whether Chrome trims feature names is not shown in the packet; both sides assert it does not. Refusing a whitespace-padded TOML key is cheap and keeps the config reading back as written, so accepting was a sound choice either way.
guidance_note: When writing a predicate that guards a joined string, write the accept/reject table first (empty, padded, separator-bearing, variable-bearing) rather than adding one clause per known bad shape.

evidence: `flags.features(...)` folds by raw table key while `_expand` runs later over the rendered switch. So `${CROM_NAMESPACE}Foo` and `appFoo` survive as distinct names and can land in both enable and disable. The agent made feature names literal (refusing `${`) instead of re-checking after expansion, which removes the case and deletes code.
guidance_note: When routing a new value through an existing expansion pass, decide explicitly whether that value should interpolate, instead of inheriting interpolation by accident.

evidence: This duplicates F3: a leading/trailing-whitespace feature name passes `name.strip()`. Chrome's trimming behavior is not established by the packet. The fix enumerates illegal names in `_ILLEGAL_FEATURE_NAMES` and refuses rather than normalizes.
guidance_note: When writing a predicate that guards a joined string, write the accept/reject table first (empty, padded, separator-bearing, variable-bearing) rather than adding one clause per known bad shape.

evidence: parse_features' comma guarantee is checked on raw text, but expansion of `${CROM_CONFIG_DIR}` could inject a comma after the check. The agent removed expansion for feature names instead of re-validating, so the parse-time guarantee holds all the way to argv.
guidance_note: When routing a new value through an existing expansion pass, decide explicitly whether that value should interpolate, instead of inheriting interpolation by accident.

evidence: As the PR stood, the features lines in `_reject_unknown_variables` were an untested failure path. The agent deleted that path, since names became literal, and tested the parse-time `${` refusal instead, which fails before `port_for` can run.
guidance_note: When adding a new failure path, add its test in the same commit.

evidence: The README listed only flags and env as interpolating, while the code expanded feature names too. The agent made the README true by making feature names literal and added 'Feature names are literal' to the features row, instead of documenting accidental behavior.
guidance_note: When a new key flows through an existing pipeline, check the README's per-key capability statements against what the pipeline now does to that key.

evidence: This is the cli.py:351 `_effective_flags` docstring instance of the stale `--disable-features` example. It is fixed with F1/F2 in 73f9e64.
guidance_note: When reserving a switch, grep comments and docstrings for that switch used as an example and update them in the same commit.

narrative: All nine findings came from round 0 against the original commit, and round 1 approved. The strongest moves were F4/F6, where the agent rejected adding a post-expansion re-check and made feature names literal instead. That one change also resolved F7 and F8 and deleted code. F3/F5 rest on an unshown claim about Chrome not trimming feature names, but refusing padded names is safe either way.
guidance_observations: Reserving a switch should come with a grep for that switch in comments and docs; three stale examples were reported separately.
The agent fixed a third stale site the reviewer had only mentioned in passing, which kept the fix from needing another round.

evidence: `del resolved[switch]` followed by a later re-insert moves the key to the end, contradicting the unchanged 'position where it was first introduced' docstring. The agent took the reviewer's first option, a docstring stating that a drop removes the position. It argued that an index map would be a second record of order, and added a test pinning where the switch lands.
guidance_note: When adding a mutation (deletion) to a structure whose docstring promises an ordering, re-read that promise and state what the new mutation does to it.

evidence: Renaming `parse_flags` to `parse_layer` left references at chrome.py:55 and test_chrome.py:99. The agent updated both and grepped the repo for `parse_flags`.
guidance_note: When renaming a function, grep the whole repo, comments included, for the old name in the same commit.

evidence: `drop_flags` was added to `_DEFAULTS_KEYS`/`_PROFILE_KEYS` with no README config-reference row. The agent added a row in 1e0b08b, and that row was incomplete: see F7 and F11.
guidance_note: When adding a user-facing config key, write its README row in the original PR, listing every refusal the parser enforces.

evidence: The docstring claims the reserved answer outranks 'carries a value' for drop_flags, but tests covered only the non-reserved valued case and the valueless reserved case. 6abcc63 added test_a_reserved_drop_carrying_a_value_is_refused_as_reserved_not_for_the_value.
guidance_note: When a docstring calls an ordering load-bearing, add a test for the input where both checks fire.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. 6abcc63 only added a test to test_config.py, and `Layer` with its disjointness docstring is original-PR code. The docstring asserted disjointness that only `config.parse_layer` enforced, unlike ProfileSpec's `__post_init__`. The agent moved the check into `Layer.__post_init__`.
guidance_note: When a type's docstring states an invariant, enforce it in the constructor as sibling types in the same file do, not only in one caller.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. The `spec.flags.sets` comparison is original-PR code, and 6abcc63 only added a test. The agent reproduced the bug: declared effective `--a=1` vs asked `--a=1 --b=2`, a spurious exit 4. The agent's planned fix broke an existing test, so it shipped a third design, applying the declaration's drops beneath the request, and checked all four shapes.
guidance_note: When adding a new half (drops) to a type compared in a convergence check, run the check with each side carrying only the half it can express and confirm equal inputs converge.

evidence: The README drop_flags row was written in 1e0b08b for F3. It listed three refusals but omitted the set-and-drop-in-one-stanza refusal that parse_layer enforces. The flag names 6abcc63, but the row came from the F3 fix.
guidance_note: When writing a reference row that enumerates refusals, derive the list from every raise in the parser, not from memory.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. `_DISCARDS_EVERY_LAYER` is in the original round-0 hunk, and 6abcc63 is test-only. The features layer is the last `compose` argument and drops only intersect earlier layers, so 'discard every layer's features at once' cannot happen. The agent corrected the reason and kept the refusal.
guidance_note: Before writing an error message that names a consequence, trace the composition order to confirm the consequence can actually happen.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 6abcc63 is test-only, and the drops exclusion comment is original. `drop_flags = ["--${CROM_PROFIL_DIR}"]` passed silently. The agent refused `${`, empty and whitespace entries at parse time, which also catches known variables like `${CROM_PORT}`. That new table later produced F11 and F12.
guidance_note: When adding a list whose entries are matched literally, apply the sibling literal-name rules (like parse_features') to it in the original PR.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. 42fe11e changed the README row and a config.py message, while the 'Sorted, because ... crom config prints this' sentence predates it in the compose docstring. The code sorts only within each layer (`sorted(one_layer.drops & resolved.keys())`), so the comment overstated the guarantee. The agent qualified it.
guidance_note: When a comment justifies a sort, state the scope the sort covers (per layer vs global).

evidence: 104e42d, the F9 fix, added `_ILLEGAL_DROPS` (empty, whitespace, `${`) to flags.drops, but the README row still listed four refusals. 4bc0a2e rewrote the row to state that an entry is a literal switch name, which is one of the reviewer's offered options.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a refusal to a parser, update the README row that enumerates its refusals in the same commit.

evidence: The F9 fix placed the `_ILLEGAL_DROPS` shape checks after the value check. So `--${FOO}=bar` is told to write `--${FOO}`, which the new rule then refuses on reload, where before the fix that remedy would have loaded. The agent moved the shape checks onto `flag.switch`, ahead of the value check, and tested that each remedy round-trips.
guidance_note: When adding a new refusal to a parser that already suggests remedies, run each existing remedy back through the new rule; this PR had already pinned that same ordering rule for reserved switches.

narrative: Most findings were real defects in original-PR code, and several ON-NAMED-FIX flags on test-only commit 6abcc63 are false positives. The fix-caused ones trace to two fixes. The F3 README row omitted a refusal (F7), and the F9 drop-entry refusal table both outdated the README (F11) and created a remedy-that-fails ordering bug (F12). F12 alone drove round 3, which an exhaustive remedy round-trip check on the F9 fix would have avoided.
guidance_observations: The agent had already written down 'a diagnostic whose remedy does not work is worse than none' for reserved switches, but did not re-apply it when adding new refusals in a fix.
On F6 the agent ran the full suite before shipping its planned fix, caught that the plan broke the omit-a-flag case, and changed course instead of trading one bug for another.
